_comment_paths: lean-trader.service runs with ProtectSystem=strict and only two ReadWritePaths: /opt/lean-engine/Launcher/bin/Release and /tmp -- every other path is read-only (not inaccessible) to this service, including /lean, which has never existed on this filesystem at all. LEAN's Initializer.Start() (Engine/Initializer.cs) unconditionally calls Directory.CreateDirectory(Globals.ResultsDestinationFolder) on startup; when results-destination-folder resolved to /lean/Results this threw System.IO.IOException: Read-only file system : '/lean' and crashed the service before the algorithm ever loaded -- this was masked for months by the (now-fixed) empty job-user-id crash, which aborted the process even earlier, before Initializer.Start() ran. results-destination-folder and transaction-log are now relative paths; LEAN resolves relative paths (Directory.CreateDirectory in Initializer.Start(), and the file write in Engine.SaveListOfTrades()) against the process's current working directory, which for this systemd unit equals WorkingDirectory=/opt/lean-engine/Launcher/bin/Release -- the one writable path. This also likely explains a previously-unexplained symptom: Globals.ResultsDestinationFolder falls back to Directory.GetCurrentDirectory() whenever Config.Get("results-destination-folder") can't be used, which is exactly bin/Release -- i.e. results writing to bin/Release instead of the intended lean/Results path. See _comment_data_provider below for why data-folder changed too.
_comment_handler_resolution: Without the five keys added directly below, lean-trader crashed on every startup with System.InvalidCastException: Unable to cast object of type 'QuantConnect.Packets.LiveNodePacket' to type 'QuantConnect.Packets.BacktestNodePacket', thrown from BacktestingResultHandler.Initialize() inside Engine.Run(). Root cause (confirmed by reading QuantConnect/Lean's current source, not guessed): Queues/JobQueue.cs builds the job packet from Globals.LiveMode, which is set directly from this file's top-level "live-mode" key -- so with live-mode:true it correctly builds a LiveNodePacket. But LeanEngineAlgorithmHandlers.FromConfiguration() resolves each handler independently via its OWN hardcoded default, e.g. Config.Get("result-handler", "BacktestingResultHandler"), Config.Get("setup-handler", "ConsoleSetupHandler"), Config.Get("data-feed-handler", "FileSystemDataFeed"), Config.Get("transaction-handler", "BacktestingTransactionHandler"), Config.Get("real-time-handler", "BacktestingRealTimeHandler") -- none of these defaults branch on live-mode at all, so with no explicit override every handler silently defaulted to its backtesting variant regardless of live-mode's value. This is NOT a LEAN regression: `git log --follow -p` on this file shows it has never once included these five keys, back to the very first commit (c38b3b6), so a flat config here could never have resolved live handlers correctly via defaults alone -- whatever produced this project's previously-reported live Alpaca fills must have supplied these keys some other way (e.g. directly in the deployed config.json on the Pi, never committed back to this template). Separately confirmed via Config.cs's GetToken(): when no "environment" key is set, GetToken() just falls through to settings.SelectToken(key) on the flat top level -- there is no requirement to nest these under an "environments" block for live-mode to work; a plain top-level key resolves identically to one merged in from a named environment. So the fix is these five additive keys, not a restructure. Values copied verbatim from LEAN's own bundled Launcher/config.json sample's "live-alpaca" environment block. See DEVIATIONS.md for the full incident writeup.
_comment_data_provider: data-provider was previously "QuantConnectDataProvider", which is not a real LEAN type -- confirmed by grepping QuantConnect/Lean's current source (Engine/DataFeeds/): the only IDataProvider implementations are DefaultDataProvider, ApiDataProvider, DownloaderDataProvider, and CompositeDataProvider. Composer.GetExportedValueByTypeName<IDataProvider>() matches only exact AssemblyQualifiedName/FullName/Name (see Extensions.MatchesTypeName), so this would have thrown 'Unable to locate any exports matching the requested typeName: QuantConnectDataProvider' and crashed on the very next startup after the /lean path fix, in LeanEngineAlgorithmHandlers.InitializeAuxiliaryDataProviders(). ApiDataProvider requires a paid, terms-accepted QuantConnect Cloud account (its ctor throws unless organization.DataAgreement.Signed) which this project deliberately avoids -- see DEVIATIONS.md 'LEAN built from source (not CLI)'. Switched to DefaultDataProvider, the same value LEAN's own bundled Launcher/config.json sample uses: it reads only from local disk under data-folder, never touches the network, and needs no account. data-folder now points at /opt/lean-engine/Data, LEAN's bundled sample market-data directory -- present on this Pi because setup/06_lean_build.sh does a full (non-sparse) `git clone` of QuantConnect/Lean, which includes Data/ (confirmed: no step deletes or excludes it afterward). That path is read-only under ProtectSystem=strict, but DefaultDataProvider only ever reads from data-folder, never writes, so no ReadWritePaths change is needed. Note: this is LEAN's own demo dataset (forex/equity/crypto samples) -- it is not verified to be complete for every symbol DualMomentumV2 actually trades. DefaultDataProvider.Fetch() returns null on a missing file rather than crashing, so this won't reproduce the read-only-filesystem crash, but historical-data completeness for the live symbols is a separate, unaddressed question outside this fix's scope.
_comment_job_user_id: job-user-id MUST be a numeric string, never empty. QuantConnect.Globals.Reset() calls Config.GetInt("job-user-id") with no default; Config.GetValue<T> only falls back to a default when the key is ABSENT from config.json, not when it is present but empty. An empty string here makes Convert.ChangeType("", typeof(int)) throw System.FormatException inside the Globals static constructor, which aborts the process (SIGABRT) before Main() ever runs. Do not revert this to "". (Note: this file is fed through Makefile's `make deploy`, which parses it with Python's json.load -- plain // comments are not valid here, hence this _comment_ sibling key instead.)
_comment_job_project_id: job-project-id is NOT read by this build of LEAN -- Globals.Reset() actually reads Config.GetInt("project-id") (no "job-" prefix). Since "project-id" is absent from this file, it silently defaults to 0, so this key is currently inert. Left as an int literal 0 (not a string) so it can never hit the same empty-string GetInt crash; renaming it to match the real key was out of scope for this fix.
